key_insight: Storage capacity of a d×d linear associative memory is governed not just by matrix degrees of freedom (d^2) but critically by the retrieval criterion: strict top-1 (winner-take-all) retrieval requires d^2 ~ n log n, while relaxed/listwise criteria permit very different scaling.
problem_solved: Determines how many key–value associations a linear memory can reliably store and retrieve under different retrieval rules, and identifies sharp capacity thresholds in an isotropic Gaussian model.
method: Model associations as isotropic Gaussian key–value pairs and analyze the correlation-matrix (superposition) memory construction.
Derive rigorous probabilistic thresholds for retrieval success under different criteria (top-1 vs listwise/shortlist), proving the logarithmic penalty for winner-take-all retrieval.
Combine random-matrix / concentration techniques to identify sharp phase transitions in capacity as a function of d and n.
impact: Clarifies fundamental trade-offs between memory size, retrieval strictness, and reliability—guiding design of associative memory modules and retrieval strategies in ML systems where shortlist vs exact-match behavior matters.
visual_elements: Schematic of a d×d memory matrix storing superposed key–value pairs (iconic keys/values being summed into the matrix).
Capacity-scaling plot: axes d^2 (storage) vs n (number of associations) showing regions where retrieval succeeds/fails and the d^2 ≈ n·log n threshold for top-1.
Comparison diagram of retrieval criteria: winner-take-all (single correct signal must beat all distractors) vs listwise/shortlist retrieval (allow top-k).
Phase/threshold map (heatmap or colored regions) illustrating sharp transitions between feasible and infeasible storage regimes.
paper_title: Sharp Capacity Thresholds in Linear Associative Memory: From Winner-Take-All to Listwise Retrieval
paper_authors: Nicholas Barnfield, Juno Kim, Eshaan Nichani, Jason D. Lee, Yue M. Lu
